- File: .github/workflows/ci.yml (and the two release gates)
  Location: lines 1451-1455 in ci.yml (and equivalents in mark-stable.yml:407-411 and test-and-mark-stable.yml:4875-4879), the no-FAIL-line branch
  Issue: When the log file `/tmp/poll_shard_${shard}.log` is missing, the script still emits the `::error::orchestrate-poll shard ${shard} had no FAIL line; last log lines follow` annotation, but the subsequent `tail` produces no output (the `|| true` masks the `tail` failure), so the annotation's "last log lines follow" promise is broken. The "produced no log" guard at lines 1421-1425 already handles the truly missing-log case, so this branch is unreachable in practice, but a defensive guard that suppresses the tail (or emits a different annotation) would avoid a misleading annotation if the file disappeared between the earlier guard and this code.
  Suggested minimal fix: After the `tail ... || true` substitution, check whether any tail lines were actually read; if not, replace the "last log lines follow" wording with a "log was unreadable" variant or skip the annotation.
  Estimated lines changed: ~6 lines
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2

- File: .github/workflows/ci.yml (and the two release gates)
  Location: lines 1446-1448 in ci.yml (FAIL-line escapes)
  Issue: The annotation escapes `%`, `\r`, `\n` per GitHub's workflow-command rules but does not escape the literal `::` sequence. GitHub's parser treats everything after the first `::command::` as data, so a FAIL-line reason that contains `::warning::foo` is not re-interpreted as a separate command in practice. Defensive depth: pre-escape `::` to `%3A%3A` (or similar) to make the parsing invariant explicit and resilient to any future change in GitHub's parser or to log content that arrives through a code path that pre-parses commands.
  Suggested minimal fix: Add `shard_fail_line="${shard_fail_line//::/%3A%3A}"` before the existing escapes.
  Estimated lines changed: 1 line
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
